Legend:
Meat-eater (eat meat, not mainly vegetarian)
Flexitarian (mainly vegetarian, but occasionally eat meat or fish)
Vegetarian (do not eat any meat, fish, or shellfish)

Percentages shown in the graph:

| Age group | Meat-eater | Flexitarian | Vegetarian |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Group A (Age 18–24) | 68% | 12% | 8% |
| Group B (Age 25–49) | 73% | 12% | 6% |
| Group C (Age 50–64) | 73% | 16% | 4% |
| Group D (Age 65+) | 77% | 13% | 3% |

Note: Data for some dietary categories are not shown, and percentages in the graph are rounded.

The above graph shows the percentages of U.K. respondents by age who self-reported their dietary choices as Meat-eater, Flexitarian, or Vegetarian, based on data released in 2026.","options":["The most common dietary choice among the respondents was Meat-eater in all age groups shown.","With respect to the category of Vegetarian, Group A, the youngest age group, showed the highest percentage among the four age groups.","In Group B, the percentage of Meat-eater was lower than 70 percent.","When it comes to the percentage of Flexitarian in each age group, the highest was in Group C.","For Group D, the oldest age group, less than five percent of the respondents reported Vegetarian as their dietary choice."],"has_visual":true,"visual_description":"A grouped vertical bar graph titled “Self-reported Dietary Choices by Age in the U.K. (2026).” The vertical axis is labeled “(%)” and has labeled ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100. Four groups appear from left to right: Group A (Age 18–24), Group B (Age 25–49), Group C (Age 50–64), and Group D (Age 65+). Each group has three adjacent bars: an unshaded bar for Meat-eater, a diagonally striped bar for Flexitarian, and a solid gray bar for Vegetarian. Percentage labels are printed above the bars. A boxed legend appears above the plotting area, and a note appears below the graph.","uncertainties":[]},{"number":26,"question":"Chuck Jones에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 <u>않는</u> 것은?","context":"Chuck Jones was an influential director and artist whose work shaped animated films and cartoon production. He was born in Spokane, Washington, in 1912, though he grew up in Los Angeles. As a child, Jones had many opportunities to draw. He used the leftover pencils and paper that his father brought him from work. Jones began his career in animation in 1930 and was quickly promoted. In the 1940s, he created famous characters such as Wile E. Coyote and the Road Runner. He directed the famous cartoon film How the Grinch Stole Christmas, which is still enjoyed by many people today. Jones started his own company, Chuck Jones Enterprises, in 1970. For his contribution to the field of animation, he received an Honorary Academy Award in 1996. Our school is holding a food waste reduction competition to promote sustainable living. This competition has been held every year since 2023. Your effort makes a difference!

When: October 1 to October 31, 2026

Who: All classes of RCQ High School will participate.

How
• Every lunch, we will give a point to each student who doesn’t leave food on their tray.
• Students’ points will be combined by class. Winning classes will be decided by each class’s points.

Prizes

|  | Number of Winners | Reward (per class) |
|---|---|---|
| 1st prize | 1 class | Snacks worth $200 |
| 2nd prize | 1 class | Snacks worth $150 |

Course Content
